q_learning.summary: A table of action values over quantile-binned market cells and the agent's position, learned by Watkins' off-policy update on the train span's reward tape.
q_learning.implementationNote: Bridge: Boltzmann share of Q(flat, long) vs Q(flat, short), temperature fitted on validation. Differs from the spec: the market does not react to the agent, so this is cost-aware reward maximisation on the train span's price tape (next-open fills, round-trip cost); values are read at the flat position so a bar's prediction does not depend on earlier calls. P(up) is the policy's long share, not a fitted probability. Price: the cell's training mean price target. Expect: values near conditional mean returns.

bin_count.label: Bin count
bin_count.description: Quantile bins per state feature, edges fitted on the training span; the market cell is the combination of the bins.

state_feature_count.label: State feature count
state_feature_count.description: Feature columns that define the market state: the ones with the largest training-span rank correlation with the tape's reward (or the price target).

learning_rate.label: Learning rate
learning_rate.description: Step size of each temporal-difference update of the table.

discount_factor.label: Discount factor
discount_factor.description: Weight of the next bar's value in the Bellman target (0 = myopic, 1 = undiscounted).

epochs.label: Epochs
epochs.description: Sweeps over the training span's tape; the sweep with the best validation log loss is kept.

patience.label: Patience
patience.description: Sweeps without a better validation log loss before training stops.

sarsa.summary: On-policy temporal-difference learning: the same table as Q-learning, bootstrapped from the action the epsilon-greedy behaviour policy actually takes next.
sarsa.implementationNote: Bridge: Boltzmann share of Q(flat, long) vs Q(flat, short), temperature fitted on validation. Differs from the spec: the market does not react to the agent, so this is cost-aware reward maximisation on the train span's price tape (next-open fills, round-trip cost); values are read at the flat position so a bar's prediction does not depend on earlier calls. P(up) is the policy's long share, not a fitted probability. Price: the cell's training mean price target. Expect: close to Q-learning; the action does not change the next bar.

dyna_q.summary: Q-learning plus a learned model of each state-action's last reward and next state, replayed for extra planning updates after every real bar.
dyna_q.implementationNote: Bridge: Boltzmann share of Q(flat, long) vs Q(flat, short), temperature fitted on validation. Differs from the spec: the market does not react to the agent, so this is cost-aware reward maximisation on the train span's price tape (next-open fills, round-trip cost); values are read at the flat position so a bar's prediction does not depend on earlier calls. P(up) is the policy's long share, not a fitted probability. Planning replays real tape outcomes. Price: the cell's training mean price target. Expect: Q-learning, converged faster.

dynamic_programming.summary: Exact backward induction over a market model estimated on the training span: k-means clusters, their counted transitions, and each cluster's mean bar moves and cost.
dynamic_programming.implementationNote: Bridge: Q0(cluster, flat, long) - Q0(cluster, flat, short) through a Boltzmann share whose temperature is fitted on validation. Differs from the spec: position is the only controlled variable; the market model (clusters, transitions, mean rewards) is estimated in-sample, the horizon ends in a flat liquidation. Expect: a discounted, cost-adjusted regime-conditional expected move.

cluster_count.label: Cluster count
cluster_count.description: Market states: k-means clusters of the state features, fitted on the training span.

state_feature_count.label: State feature count
state_feature_count.description: Feature columns that define the market state: the ones with the largest training-span rank correlation with the tape's reward (or the price target).

discount_factor.label: Discount factor
discount_factor.description: Weight of the next bar's value in the Bellman target (0 = myopic, 1 = undiscounted).

planning_horizon.label: Planning horizon
planning_horizon.description: Steps the planner looks ahead; 0 uses the run's label horizon.

additive_smoothing.label: Additive smoothing
additive_smoothing.description: Pseudo-counts added to every transition and state mean, so a rare state leans on the prior instead of a handful of bars.

monte_carlo_tree_search.summary: UCT search at every bar over position sequences, simulating the training span's cluster Markov model with rewards resampled from each cluster's own bars.
monte_carlo_tree_search.implementationNote: Bridge: the root's mean return of long minus short through a Boltzmann share, temperature fitted on validation; the root splits its simulations evenly, each bar's search is seeded by the bar. Differs from the spec: the simulator is a market model fitted on the same training span, and the market does not react to the agent. Expect: that model's expected-return ranking re-derived with sampling noise.

additive_smoothing.label: Additive smoothing

zero_sum_game.summary: Per market cluster, a zero-sum matrix game of the trader (short, flat, long) against a market that picks the outcome distribution, solved exactly by the minimax linear program.
zero_sum_game.implementationNote: Bridge: the equilibrium expected position through a Boltzmann share, temperature fitted on validation. Differs from the spec: the spec ranks decisions rather than forecasting; the market is not a strategic player, so it may only shift probability within a total-variation radius of the cluster's training outcomes. Expect: the regime's worst-case edge sign; mixing only at ties.

ambiguity_radius.label: Ambiguity radius
ambiguity_radius.description: Probability mass the adversarial market may move between outcome bins (a total-variation radius around the regime's empirical distribution).

additive_smoothing.label: Additive smoothing

utility_theory.summary: Per market cluster, the position in [-1, 1] that maximises expected utility (CRRA, CARA) or the cumulative-prospect-theory value of the cluster's training outcomes net of cost.
utility_theory.implementationNote: Bridge: the optimal position through a Boltzmann share, temperature fitted on validation. Differs from the spec: the spec ranks decisions rather than forecasting; the lottery is each cluster's training-span outcomes, and the risk parameters are set, not fitted to revealed choices. Price: the cluster's mean price target. Expect: a regime-conditional mean-variance rule shaped by risk preference.

utility_form.label: Utility form
utility_form.description: Constant relative risk aversion, constant absolute risk aversion, or cumulative prospect theory.

risk_aversion.label: Risk aversion
risk_aversion.description: The CRRA coefficient (1 = log utility, the Kelly case) or the CARA coefficient per unit of wealth.

exposure_fraction.label: Exposure fraction
exposure_fraction.description: Wealth change per unit position per unit of the scaled h-bar move (the lottery's stake).

loss_aversion.label: Loss aversion
loss_aversion.description: Prospect theory: how much more a loss weighs than an equal gain.

value_curvature.label: Value curvature
value_curvature.description: Prospect theory: the power of the value function on gains and losses.

probability_weighting.label: Probability weighting
probability_weighting.description: Prospect theory: the Tversky-Kahneman weighting exponent (1 = no distortion).

additive_smoothing.label: Additive smoothing
additive_smoothing.description: Pseudo-counts added to every transition and state mean, so a rare state leans on the prior instead of a handful of bars.

markov_decision_process.summary: A discounted Markov decision process over (market cluster, position): transitions and rewards counted from the training span's tape, solved by value iteration.
markov_decision_process.implementationNote: Bridge: Q*(cluster, flat, long) - Q*(cluster, flat, short) through a Boltzmann share, temperature fitted on validation. Differs from the spec: the market does not react to the agent, so this is cost-aware reward maximisation on the train span's price tape (next-open fills, round-trip cost); values are read at the flat position so a bar's prediction does not depend on earlier calls. P(up) is the policy's long share, not a fitted probability. Expect: a cost-aware regime drift.

convergence_tolerance.description: Value iteration stops when no state value moves by more than this.

markov_chain.summary: A higher-order Markov chain over buckets of the scaled one-bar move, with counted, smoothed transitions; h-step paths simulated from each state give its up-share.
markov_chain.implementationNote: Bridge: P(up) is the share of simulated h-bar paths that end up, per chain state. Differs from the spec: the state is built from the bar-return series (closes), not the feature row; direction needs h steps, so the table is simulated, not read off P^n, with the training drift removed by default. Price: the mean simulated cumulative move. Expect: near 0.5 except where recent moves are extreme.

bin_count.label: Bin count
bin_count.description: Buckets of the scaled one-bar move (the chain's states per step), edges fitted on the training span.

markov_order.label: Markov order
markov_order.description: How many past buckets define the chain state (a higher-order chain). Not searched: it sets the history the model needs.

additive_smoothing.label: Additive smoothing
additive_smoothing.description: Pseudo-counts added to every transition and state mean, so a rare state leans on the prior instead of a handful of bars.

path_count.label: Path count
path_count.description: Simulated h-step paths per chain state for the up-share table.

remove_training_drift.label: Remove training drift
remove_training_drift.description: Centre the simulated moves on the training span's mean move, so the table carries the chain's serial dependence rather than one window's drift.
